full_judgment:
16. Rule 143 provides the inquiry procedure in cases of negligence, inefficiency, misconduct and corruption, etc. and in order to avoid Rule 143 the respondent has purposely chosen Rule 150 sub-rule 1 with a malafide intention to deprive the petitioner of his right of due process of law which is a right to be dealt with in accordance with law and only in accordance with law as guaranteed by Article 31 of our Constitution. Article 31 of our Constitution guaranteed every citizen the right of due protection of law and by taking resort to Rule 150 the authority has abused the process of the Rule by-passing Rule 143 which contemplated prior inquiry in accordance with law. 

 23. In the instant case although the service of the petitioner has been terminated and termination is not a penalty within the meaning of Rule 139, nonetheless the petitioner has lost his job and this termination can be well construed as removal from service under Rule 139-G because the termination has been given on the ground of inefficiency which is a ground of penalty under Rule 138. The authority wilfully avoided the normal procedure of Rules 138, 139 and 143 and arbitrarily resorted to Rule 150 and in that case also 3 month notice of termination was not given and instead 3 month salary was given depriving him of any right to move the higher authority under sub-rule 4(b) for review and sub-rule 5 for appeal because that right could be exercised only by these employees upon whom notice under sub-rule 1 or 2 has been served. This is obviously colorable exercise of power which is malafide and unreasonable and devoid of any reasons. The authority could not show that it has before it sufficient materials to satisfy itself about the inefficiency and the authority applied its mind to those and had objective satisfaction in taking drastic action as has been done by Annexure ''B''.
